subject: design-technology
title: Cams & Cranks
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: cams, followers, crank slider mechanisms.
final_note: Cams and cranks change rotation into other motion.

concepts.def: Shaped wheel that lifts a follower.
Part that moves up as cam rotates.
Bent shaft used to convert motion.

walkthroughs.body_html: The four types of motion: rotary (spinning), linear (straight line), reciprocating (back and forth), oscillating (swinging like a pendulum).
A cam is a non-circular wheel. As it spins, a follower rides up and down its edge — turning rotary motion into reciprocating. Old toys and automata use cams.
A crank slider takes the spinning of an engine and turns it into the straight push-pull of a piston (or the other way). Bike pedals are also cranks.
